source.title: Thermal Mining of Ices on Cold Solar System Bodies: NIAC Phase I Final Report
source.author: George Sowers, Colorado School of Mines
source.page_convention: Printed page number equals one-based PDF page number; PDF contains 135 pages.
source.real_or_nominal: Not identified in the reconstructed source section; retain unadjusted printed dollars.

operating_years.source: p.81 ground rules: ten-year operational life

learning_curve_ratio.source: p.72 calls 0.9 an exponent; Table 4.8.7 values support 90% unit learning, exponent log2(0.9)

nonrecurring_cost_multiplier.source: p.85 sensitivity applies a cost factor to every non-recurring element; baseline factor one

cost_mode.source: Default uses Table 4.9.3 directly; alternatives reconstruct component costs and scale.

revenue_mode.source: Default preserves Table 4.9.3 revenue even where inconsistent with Table 4.9.2 demand.

nasa_savings_mode.source: Default preserves rounded $5185M incremental Mars saving on p.86.

mars_first_operating_year.source: p.81 last paragraph: Mars demand begins in third operating year

demand_multiplier.source: Default one preserves Table 4.9.2; override is a controlled demand experiment, not a new historical input.

annual_revenue_musd.source: Overrides the full-demand Table 4.9.3 revenue at source price before price/demand multipliers.

discount_rate.source: Not specified for the native IRR calculation; NPV only exists when a caller supplies both rate and cash-flow timing.

development_subsystems_source: Reported inputs: p.72 Table 4.8.6; dollar entries converted from printed $k where necessary.
production_subsystems_source: Reported inputs: p.73 Table 4.8.7; totals multiplied by 1000 from printed $k.

production_subsystems.name: Ice hauler bases including GPV base

launch.source: p.74 section 4.8.4, Tables 4.8.8-4.8.9; reported assumptions and inferred allocation arithmetic

commercial.source: pp.81-84; case parameters and outputs from Table 4.9.3; scale from p.83

ppp_lunar.source: pp.81-84; case parameters and outputs from Table 4.9.3; scale from p.83

ppp_lunar_mars.source: pp.81-84; case parameters and outputs from Table 4.9.3; scale from p.83; Mars demand starts operating year 3 per p.81

demand_segments.name: Mars hardware transport propellant
demand_segments.source: p.82 Table 4.9.2; this demand is propulsion for hardware delivery, not the 75t hardware itself

nasa_savings.source: pp.85-87: government savings calculation; reported inputs, unadjusted dollars

reported_table.description: Preserve printed Table 4.9.3 costs and plateau revenue, including $971M Mars revenue. This is the default historical reporting branch.

demand_revenue.description: Keep printed Table 4.9.3 costs, derive revenue from Table 4.9.2 surface demand and price. Mars plateau is $941M. Explicit alternative, not a correction to the archived source.

prose_scaled_costs.description: Reconstruct section 4.8 costs and apply p.83 printed factors 1/1.052/1.625; derive revenue from demand. Fractional launch allocation retained before rounding.

demand_ratio_scaled_costs.description: Replace inconsistent printed scales with production/base-production ratios, using the stated proportional scaling rule; retain additional discrete Mars launch. Explicit alternative.

illustrative_uniform_annual.provenance: Analyst timing scenario only, not recovered source cash flows. Four equal annual development/build installments (p.81 duration); two equal deployment-year installments approximating 18 months; five equal public-investment installments (p.82 five-year POP). Operations in figure-style years 7-16; exact phasing is not published. No tuning to the IRRs.

unresolved: Annual or milestone phasing of development, build, deployment and NASA payments is not tabulated.
Partial initial and final production years cannot be uniquely inferred from the plotted cash-flow curves.
No explicit tax, depreciation, working-capital, debt, terminal-value or replacement cash-flow schedules are supplied in section 4.9; none are fabricated.
Currency year and real/nominal treatment are not identified here.
NASA net-savings headlines do not exactly follow the printed annual figures, ten-year life and third-year Mars onset.
